request.spec:
When a claim is opened it receives the next number on the sheet: 1 for the first claim ever
opened on the sheet, then 2, and so on, with no gaps and never reused, even when two users open
claims at the same moment. A draft has no number, and voiding a claim clears its number (the
number is not given to anyone else). Show the number on the claim. Every audit line about a
claim that has a number gains number=<number> at its end (so CLAIM_OPENED and CLAIM_SETTLED
carry it; a CLAIM_VOIDED line carries the number the claim had).

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
When a claim is opened it receives the next number on the sheet: 1 for the first claim ever
opened on the sheet, then 2, and so on, with no gaps and never reused, even when two users open
claims at the same moment. A draft has no number, and voiding a claim clears its number (the
number is not given to anyone else). Show the number on the claim. Every audit line about a
claim that has a number gains number=<number> at its end (so CLAIM_OPENED and CLAIM_SETTLED
carry it; a CLAIM_VOIDED line carries the number the claim had).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Claims are now numbered when they're opened. `bin/e2e` builds and passes all 4 tests, including the one where two users open claims at the same moment.

**Stored data** — new migration `V7__claim_number.sql`:
- Each claim gets a `number` column, and each sheet gets a `claim_numbers` counter of how many numbers it has handed out.
- No two claims on a sheet can share a number: a unique index on `(sheet_id, number)` blocks it.
- Claims that were already OPEN or SETTLED are numbered in the order they were created. That backfill doesn't matter here, since the database is in-memory and starts empty on every run.

**Server**
- **Opening a claim** takes the next number from the sheet's counter in the same transaction (`Sheets.nextClaimNumber`). Adding one to the counter locks the sheet's row until the transaction ends, so two openings at once queue up and get different numbers. There are no gaps, and a number is never reused.
- **Same claim, two users:** loading a claim now locks its row too. If two people act on the same claim at once, the changes happen one after the other, so a claim can't be opened twice and use up two numbers.
- **Voiding** clears the claim's number. The CLAIM_VOIDED line still ends with the number it had, and a draft voided without ever being opened gets no `number=`. That old number goes through a small new `ClaimNumber` record (`ApplyClaimStatus` sets it, `RecordClaimStatusChanged` reads it).
- **Audit lines:** CLAIM_OPENED and CLAIM_SETTLED end with `number=<n>`. A claim can be edited at any status, so CLAIM_EDITED also ends with `number=<n>` when the claim has one. That follows "every audit line about a claim that has a number". The tests only edit unnumbered claims, so that case isn't exercised.
- The claim's number (or null) is now part of what the server sends for each claim.

**Front end** — each claim row shows its number in `claim-number`, and it's empty for drafts and voided claims.
